% Generated by task tex-boundary from dossiers/boundary-adaptor.md, sections B, C, D and F.
% Breakable inline code for this fragment's tables and prose (LuaLaTeX): \bndc{...} sets its
% argument verbatim in the monospace font, with break points after punctuation and between the
% words of a camel-case identifier. Defined once, whichever boundary fragment is read first.
\ifdefined\bndc\else
\directlua{
  bndbreak = function(s)
    local bs = string.char(92)
    local hash = string.char(35)
    s = s:gsub(hash .. hash, hash)
    local after = { ["."] = true, ["_"] = true, ["/"] = true, [":"] = true, [","] = true,
      ["-"] = true, [")"] = true, ["]"] = true, ["="] = true, ["|"] = true }
    local prev = ""
    for _, c in utf8.codes(s) do
      local ch = utf8.char(c)
      if ch:match("^[A-Z]$") and prev:match("^[a-z]$") then
        tex.sprint(bs .. "penalty400{}")
      end
      tex.sprint(-2, ch)
      if after[ch] or c > 127 then
        tex.sprint(bs .. "allowbreak{}")
      end
      prev = ch
    end
  end
}
\newcommand{\bndc}[1]{\texttt{\directlua{bndbreak("\luaescapestring{\detokenize{#1}}")}}}

\subsubsection{A different program or input?}\label{sec:gen-boundary-other-program}

Within one instantiation, no: \bndc{prog} and \bndc{input} are the same variables in
\bndc{verify prog input proof}, \bndc{verify_iff_compiled}, \bndc{leanIsaInstance prog s},
\bndc{satisfiedBy_witnessOf}, \bndc{SatisfiedBy prog input} and \bndc{ValidExecution prog input}.
Every theorem of the chain is universally quantified over both outside any probability, and the
built code confirms the shape: \bndc{piop_rbrKnowledgeSoundness (P : Phases I) (S : P.Security)}
is stated for a fixed \bndc{I} (\bndc{Spine/Compose.lean:172-177}), and ArkLib's game fixes
\bndc{stmtIn} before the prover runs (\bndc{Security/Basic.lean:299-323}:
\bndc{∀ stmtIn : StmtIn, ∀ witIn, ∀ prover, Pr[…] ≤ ε}). Three observations on the edges of that
answer:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{The program is bound by the transcript only through its stacked table.} The Lean
  side holds \bndc{prog : Program} (typed instructions, \bndc{Instruction.lean:87-93}) and
  \bndc{FsState.seed prog input} must hash \bndc{bytecodeColumn prog}
  (\bndc{FixedColumns.lean:78-82}), as the Rust hashes \bndc{bytecode_table}
  (\bndc{cpu/mod.rs:73-76, 89}). That \bndc{prog ↦ (prog.logSize, bytecodeColumn prog)} is
  injective follows from \bndc{entry_injective} (\bndc{Bytecode.lean:240-245}) and
  \bndc{bytecodeColumn_slot} (\bndc{FixedColumns.lean:84-87}); it is not stated anywhere and
  Layer 12 will need it for \enquote{statement binding} (\bndc{architecture.md:453-454}).
  Unverified: no probe was written for the lemma.
\item \textbf{\bndc{Program} and \bndc{PublicInput} are narrower than the deployed surfaces.} The
  Rust verifier takes \bndc{Vec<Op>} with \bndc{u32} operands; Lean's operands are any \bndc{K}
  (a superset); the Python takes any \bndc{K}-array (\bndc{verifier.py:1365}), including
  undecodable entries, of which Lean has none (the faithfulness review's row 4,
  \bndc{docs/reviews/leanvm-faithfulness-review.md:72}). A public input with a nonzero third limb
  is rejected by the Rust (\bndc{cpu/mod.rs:141-143}) and by the Python's \bndc{Digest}
  (\bndc{verifier.py:223}), and cannot be written in Lean (\bndc{PublicInput} is four lanes of
  \bndc{K}, \bndc{Memory.lean:101-104}). So two of \bndc{read_public}'s eight checks (leanISA's
  numbering, \bndc{Statement.lean:71-73}) are discharged \enquote{by type} on the Lean side,
  which means: by whoever parses bytes into \bndc{Program} and \bndc{PublicInput}. The
  blueprint's \emph{Verifier shape} convention (\bndc{bp:326}) says structure checks the Rust
  \bndc{assert!}s are \enquote{theorems about the layout, not branches of \bndc{verify}}; it does
  not say that these two are parsing obligations of the fixture harness and, later, of
  end-to-end soundness's (T7) \bndc{PublicInput.encode} (\cref{f:boundary-parse}).
\item \textbf{The sizes are the prover's}, and this is where the family of instances is
  quantified. \bndc{verify_iff_compiled} (\bndc{bp:1218-1221}) has
  \bndc{∃ s, s.Admissible prog ∧ …}; the prover writes \bndc{log_mem}, six \bndc{τ_j} and
  \bndc{log_inv_rate} onto the stream (\bndc{announce_public}, \bndc{cpu/mod.rs:118-124}) and the
  verifier reads and checks them before anything else (\bndc{read_public},
  \bndc{cpu/mod.rs:144-176}; the Python, \bndc{verifier.py:1372-1379}).
  \Cref{sec:gen-boundary-sizes-exists} takes this up.
\end{enumerate}

\subsubsection{Is \texorpdfstring{\protect\code{∃ s}}{the existential over the sizes} sound, and who checks?}\label{sec:gen-boundary-sizes-exists}

\paragraph{For the conclusion, yes.} \bndc{satisfiedBy_witnessOf} is stated for every admissible
\bndc{s}, and its conclusion \bndc{SatisfiedBy prog input (witnessOf prog s q)} does not mention
\bndc{s}; so whatever sizes the prover announces, an accepting transcript whose extracted stack
satisfies \bndc{M3Holds (leanIsaInstance prog s) input q} yields a satisfying witness and,
through \bndc{constraintSoundness}, an execution. Admissibility is checked by the verifier: the
Rust rejects \bndc{log_mem ∉ [16, 32]}, \bndc{τ_j > 32}, \bndc{τ_5 < 3}, an invalid rate, and
\bndc{μ ∉ [15, 28]} (\bndc{cpu/mod.rs:157-176}); the Python checks the rate and the \bndc{μ}
window (\bndc{verifier.py:1377-1379}) and the rest through its layout (the bus dossier
re-examined the status file's claim that it omits four caps, \cref{f:bus-status-python-caps}).
The hypothesis \bndc{hs : s.Admissible prog} of the adaptor is therefore discharged by a verifier
check, as the blueprint says (\bndc{bp:824-831}).

\paragraph{For the probability, the blueprint does not say how.} \bndc{verify_knowledgeSound} is
sketched with error \bndc{niError s Q} (\bndc{bp:1226-1227}), a function of \bndc{s}; the oracle
protocol is \enquote{a family indexed by them} (acceptance test 21, \emph{Sizes are parameters},
\bndc{bp:1326-1328}); and the per-instance theorems (\bndc{piop_rbrKnowledgeSoundness} for one
\bndc{I}, \bndc{FiatShamirSecurity} for one compiled protocol) bound the event for one \bndc{s}.
A prover against \bndc{verify} chooses \bndc{s} inside its proof, after its random-oracle
queries. Two ways to compose exist and they differ by about $2^{34}$:
\begin{itemize}
\item a union over the admissible sizes:
  \bndc{Pr[verify accepts ∧ bad] ≤ Σ_s Pr[accepts with s ∧ bad_s] ≤ Σ_s ε_s}, with
  \bndc{|{admissible s}| ≤ 11 · 28^5 · 25 · 4 ≈ 2^34} (\bndc{log_mem ≤ 26} and \bndc{τ_j ≤ 28}
  once \bndc{μ ≤ 28} is imposed; \bndc{τ_5 ≥ 3}; four rates), which the numeric target of
  acceptance test 23 (\bndc{< 2^-150}) absorbs for the oracle protocol but the 128-bit WHIR budget
  (\bndc{SECURITY_BITS}, \bndc{leaf.rs:143-145}) does not;
\item the standard argument, \bndc{Q · max_s ε_s}: each random-oracle query commits to one
  \bndc{s} because the sizes are absorbed into the chain before any challenge
  (\bndc{announce_public}; acceptance test 12, \emph{Absorb before squeeze}). This needs the
  sizes to be part of the statement the Fiat--Shamir transform hashes, that is, one protocol
  whose first prover message is \bndc{s}, on which the rest of the schedule depends. ArkLib's
  \bndc{ProtocolSpec n} has a fixed \bndc{n} and fixed message types
  (\file{ProtocolSpec/Basic.lean}), so that protocol cannot be written at the pin; the family is
  the only shape available, and \bndc{FiatShamirSecurity} must then be stated for the family
  (the challenge oracle implemented by one BLAKE2s chain shared across \bndc{s}, with \bndc{s} in
  every query), not for one instance.
\end{itemize}
\Cref{f:boundary-announced-sizes} asks the blueprint to say which, and to make \bndc{niError}
independent of the prover's choice (a maximum over admissible \bndc{s}, or the union). Either way
the \emph{conclusion} of the base theorem (T4) is unaffected; the \emph{number} is. The count of
admissible size vectors is a hand estimate from the caps and the stacking window; the exact count
depends on the layout's \bndc{μ}, which Layer 3 defines.

\paragraph{A remark for end-to-end soundness (T7).} ArkLib's game fixes the statement before the
prover runs. For end-to-end soundness (\bndc{architecture.md:339-369}) the public input is
\bndc{PublicInput.encode (FinalProof.metadata proof) expectedStatement}, part of which the prover
chooses; that needs adaptive soundness in the statement, which the deployed transcript provides
(the input seeds the chain) and which no theorem of the blueprint states
(\cref{f:boundary-non-adaptive}).

\subsubsection{Hypotheses, and where each is discharged}\label{sec:gen-boundary-hypotheses}

\begin{sloppypar}
The chain in the soundness direction:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \bndc{verify prog input proof = true};
\item by \bndc{verify_iff_compiled}: \bndc{∃ s, s.Admissible prog ∧} the Fiat--Shamir-compiled
  oracle verifier of \bndc{leanIsaInstance prog s} accepts;
\item by \bndc{verify_knowledgeSound}, in the random-oracle model: the extracted stack \bndc{q}
  satisfies \bndc{M3Holds (leanIsaInstance prog s) input q} except with probability
  \bndc{niError};
\item by \bndc{satisfiedBy_witnessOf}: \bndc{SatisfiedBy prog input (witnessOf prog s q)};
\item by \bndc{constraintSoundness}:
  \bndc{∃ t, AssignmentRepresents (witnessOf prog s q) t ∧ ValidExecution prog input t}.
\end{enumerate}
In the completeness direction:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \bndc{ValidExecution prog input t};
\item by \bndc{constraintCompleteness}: \bndc{∃ w, SatisfiedBy prog input w ∧ AssignmentRepresents w t};
\item by \bndc{Sizes.ofWitness} and \bndc{stackOf gen}:
  \bndc{M3Holds (leanIsaInstance prog s) input (stackOf gen w hs)};
\item by \bndc{piop_perfectCompleteness} and the compilation:
  \bndc{verify prog input (prove …) = true}.
\end{enumerate}
\end{sloppypar}

\Cref{tab:gen-boundary-hypotheses} lists every hypothesis on the chain, of four kinds: a
condition on \emph{public data} anyone can check; a property the \emph{verifier checks}; a
theorem another roadmap or library \emph{owes}; and one that \emph{nothing} discharges.

the bytecode is decodable and of power-of-two length at most \bndc{2^32} & \bndc{read_public} (\bndc{cpu/mod.rs:157-159}); the Python accepts any array & verifier check in the Rust; by type in Lean (\bndc{Program}, \bndc{Instruction.lean:87-93}) & the loader of \bndc{Program} & consistent; coverage gap recorded (\bndc{leanvm-faithfulness-review.md:72}) \\\addlinespace[3pt]
\bndc{κ < 64} for \bndc{MemImage.read_gpow} & inside \bndc{satisfiedBy_witnessOf}'s \bndc{word0_eq} & verifier check & from \bndc{s.Admissible prog} (\bndc{logMem ≤ 32}) & consistent \\\addlinespace[3pt]
the count columns are exactly the pulls' count coordinates & \bndc{counts_nonzero} both ways & owed by Layers 2 and 3 & a transcription from the Rust (the blueprint's category B) of \bndc{count_columns()} per table (\bndc{layout.rs:412-414}), which \bndc{Component.toM3} cannot derive from \bndc{(sep, dir)} alone & unspecified (\cref{f:boundary-witnessof-input-counts}) \\\addlinespace[3pt]
\end{longtable}}
\end{landscape}

\paragraph{Violations of the boundary.} Of the rule \enquote{nothing is assumed on one side of the
boundary which the other side does not prove}, the rows left undischarged that are not heuristics
are four: \bndc{WellFormedBytecode} (the proof system assumes nothing of it and the
arithmetization requires it), the resource bounds and the constructed witness of completeness
(the proof system's completeness theorem requires what the arithmetization's does not give), and
the Flock consequence lemma (the adaptor consumes a theorem no interface carries). The
random-oracle heuristic is a fifth, inherent, and must simply be written down.

\subsubsection{The top limb of the public input, along the whole chain}\label{sec:gen-boundary-toplimb}
% The probe's line numbers are those of probes/boundary-adaptor/Shapes.lean; the dossier cites
% them as 45-49, 51-55, 57-63, twelve lines too low (checked against the file).

The public-input dossier (\file{code-pubinput.md}, section D) traced the limb through the phase,
the spine and the deployed verifiers; this walk adds the two ends of the chain and the anchors.
Its facts used here: the oracle protocol's theorems hold for every instance, so a leanISA
instance with two lines is as good an \bndc{M3Instance} as one with three (its D.1); the deployed
verifiers pool the third claim at \bndc{0} with no scalar (\bndc{cpu/mod.rs:746, 756},
\bndc{bind_pi_claim} \bndc{cpu/mod.rs:674-682}; \bndc{verifier.py:1399-1401}; its D.3).

\begin{sloppypar}
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{The type.} \bndc{PublicInput} is four lanes of \bndc{K}, and the two words are
  built with a literal zero top limb:
\begin{leancode}
structure PublicInput where
  lanes : Fin 4 → K
  deriving DecidableEq
def PublicInput.word0 (p : PublicInput) : E := E.ofLimbs (p.lanes 0) (p.lanes 1) 0
def PublicInput.word1 (p : PublicInput) : E := E.ofLimbs (p.lanes 2) (p.lanes 3) 0
\end{leancode}
\src{LeanerVM/Semantics/Memory.lean:101-110 at b435631, docstrings omitted (probe Shapes prints them, output lines 69--78)}
  A public input with a nonzero top limb cannot be written; the probe proves
  \bndc{p.word0.limb 2 = 0} and \bndc{p.word1.limb 2 = 0} for every \bndc{p} by \bndc{simp}
  (\bndc{Shapes.lean:57-61}, exit 0). The specification agrees, \enquote{two 192-bit words (with
  top limb 0)} (\bndc{doc/leanvm/body/08-end-to-end-protocol.tex:29}), the Rust rejects a third
  limb (\bndc{cpu/mod.rs:141-143}) and the Python's \bndc{Digest} has none
  (\bndc{verifier.py:223}).
\item \textbf{What \bndc{SatisfiedBy} says of cells 0 and 1.}
  \bndc{word0_eq : (imageOf w.data).2.read (gpow 0) = some input.word0} and \bndc{word1_eq}
  (\bndc{Statement.lean:338-340}): the \emph{whole} \bndc{E}-word of the image at index 0 is
  \bndc{input.word0}, top limb included; and \bndc{public_input_eq} (\bndc{Statement.lean:315}),
  which no component reads.
\item \textbf{What \bndc{ValidExecution} says.} \bndc{HasPublicBoundary input t} has the same two
  equations on \bndc{t.image} (\bndc{Execution.lean:108-110}), whole words again.
\item \textbf{What the instance says.} Three lines (\bndc{bp:834-836}): \bndc{mem_0} with cells
  \bndc{(word0.limb 0, word1.limb 0)}, \bndc{mem_1} with \bndc{(word0.limb 1, word1.limb 1)},
  \bndc{mem_2} with \bndc{(0, 0)}. \bndc{PublicLinesHold} on them is exactly the six limb
  equalities, from which \bndc{E.ofLimbs mem_0[i] mem_1[i] mem_2[i] = input.word_i} follows
  (probe \bndc{Shapes.lean:71-76}).
\item \textbf{If the instance omitted the third line.} \bndc{M3Holds} would say nothing of
  \bndc{mem_2[0]}, \bndc{mem_2[1]}; the master theorems hold unchanged; the theorem left without a
  proof is \textbf{\bndc{satisfiedBy_witnessOf}}, for \emph{every} possible \bndc{witnessOf}, not
  only the natural one:
  \begin{itemize}
  \item the natural \bndc{witnessOf} writes the image's word 0 as
    \bndc{E.ofLimbs mem_0[0] mem_1[0] mem_2[0]}; with \bndc{mem_2[0] ≠ 0} it is not
    \bndc{input.word0}, whatever \bndc{input} (probe \bndc{Shapes.lean:63-69}:
    \bndc{E.ofLimbs a b c ≠ p.word0} when \bndc{c ≠ 0}, by comparing limb 2);
  \item a \bndc{witnessOf} that zeroed the limb when building the data and the block would break
    \bndc{mem_balanced} for any program that reads cell 0 (the reading row's pulled tuple carries
    \bndc{mem_2[0]} from \bndc{q}, the built seed carries \bndc{0});
  \item and no \bndc{witnessOf} at all can serve when no satisfying witness exists: take the
    program whose first instruction is \bndc{SET_CONSTANT [g^0, y²]}
    (\bndc{Instr.setConstant 1 (E.ofLimbs 0 0 1)}; at \bndc{fp = 1} the operand \bndc{g^0} names
    cell 0) followed by a jump to the sentinel and the fill blocks. Its constraints are
    satisfiable only with cell 0 \bndc{= y²}, whose low limbs are \bndc{0, 0}: a stack with
    \bndc{mem_0[0] = mem_1[0] = 0}, \bndc{mem_2[0] = 1} satisfies the constraints, the balances,
    the counts and the two remaining lines at \bndc{input = ⟨![0, 0, l₂, l₃]⟩}, so it is in the
    two-line \bndc{M3Holds}; but \bndc{SatisfiedBy prog input w} demands \bndc{word0_eq} with
    \bndc{input.word0 = E.ofLimbs 0 0 0 ≠ y²}, and \bndc{ValidExecution} demands the same of
    \bndc{t.image}, so neither has an inhabitant. (An inference from the definitions:
    \bndc{execute} of \bndc{SET_CONSTANT} requires \bndc{[o] = k}, \file{Step.lean}; the
    two-line stack of that program was not built as a probe; the load-bearing fact,
    \bndc{E.ofLimbs a b c ≠ p.word0} for \bndc{c ≠ 0}, is proved by the probe \bndc{Shapes}.)
  \end{itemize}
\item \textbf{If \bndc{SatisfiedBy} were weakened instead} (its two word conjuncts restricted to
  limbs 0 and 1), \bndc{satisfiedBy_witnessOf} would close with two lines, and the theorem left
  without a proof would be \textbf{\bndc{constraintSoundness}}: it must produce
  \bndc{∃ t, AssignmentRepresents w t ∧ ValidExecution prog input t}, \bndc{AssignmentRepresents}
  fixes \bndc{t.image} to \bndc{imageOf w.data} (\bndc{Statement.lean:355-362},
  \bndc{assignmentRepresents_image}), and \bndc{HasPublicBoundary} then demands the whole word
  (\bndc{Execution.lean:110}). For the program above no \bndc{t} exists, so the theorem is false.
\item \textbf{If \bndc{HasPublicBoundary} were weakened too}, nothing on the chain would object,
  and the anchor would be the specification alone; the top limb would then be constrained only
  where a guest reads it (guest correctness, T3).
\item \textbf{The anchor} is therefore the pair \bndc{PublicInput.word0},
  \bndc{PublicInput.word1} with their literal \bndc{0} (\bndc{Memory.lean:107-110}), consumed
  verbatim by \bndc{HasPublicBoundary} and by \bndc{SatisfiedBy}. The requirement of the owner's
  note (\enquote{a missing, weak or wrong verifier check must leave knowledge soundness or
  completeness unprovable}) is met one level down from the oracle protocol, in the adaptor's
  theorem, and the acceptance test that claims it (test 10, \emph{Top limb of the public input},
  \bndc{bp:1293-1295}) should name that theorem, as the public-input dossier also asks
  (\file{code-pubinput.md}, G.3). This agrees with that dossier's section D.
\end{enumerate}
\end{sloppypar}

\paragraph{The three divergences.} The obligation map is not met by the blueprint on three points:
\begin{enumerate}
\item the completeness dual composes constraint completeness (T1-C), not witness generation
  (T2), as \bndc{architecture.md:273-275} asks (\enquote{composes T2 with the honest prover});
\item it records no resource conditions, although two are load-bearing
  (\cref{f:boundary-base-completeness});
\item the hash assumption, BLAKE2s as a random oracle, is nowhere an explicit hypothesis
  (\cref{f:boundary-base-soundness}).
\end{enumerate}
Obligations of the map with no counterpart in the blueprint are these three and the
statement-binding lemma. Blueprint layers that serve no obligation of the base theorem: none
(every layer feeds \bndc{verify} or a theorem about it); three named declarations serve nothing
on the chain and are tests of non-vacuity or candidates for upstream: \bndc{witnessOf_stackOf}
(\cref{sec:gen-boundary-st-stackof}), \bndc{Extractor.Straightline.map} (no possible consumer in
this repository, \cref{sec:gen-boundary-st-composition}), \bndc{piop_rbrKnowledgeSoundness_exists}.

\paragraph{The extracted witness.} One more point of the architecture the blueprint's base
theorem loses: \enquote{the extracted leanVM witness should contain ordered \bndc{pc}/\bndc{fp}
steps and the full memory image} (\bndc{architecture.md:332-335}, for recursion, T6). The chain
has it, \bndc{constraintSoundness} giving \bndc{AssignmentRepresents (witnessOf prog s q) t} for
the extracted \bndc{q}; \bndc{baseVerifier_extractsExecution} keeps only
\bndc{∃ t, ValidExecution prog input t} (\bndc{bp:1247-1248}), which is a language membership and
needs no extractor at all. Stating the pointwise theorem in the form \enquote{for the extractor's
\bndc{q}, when it satisfies \bndc{M3Holds},
\bndc{∃ t, AssignmentRepresents (witnessOf prog s q) t ∧ ValidExecution prog input t}} costs
nothing and is what recursion consumes (\cref{f:boundary-extracted-witness}).

\subsubsection{What was checked and found consistent}\label{sec:gen-boundary-negative}

\begin{sloppypar}
\begin{itemize}
\item \bndc{M3Holds}'s five clauses against \bndc{SatisfiedBy}'s thirteen conjuncts: every conjunct
  has a source (\cref{tab:gen-boundary-conjuncts}); no conjunct of \bndc{SatisfiedBy} is delivered
  by nothing once the caps hypothesis, the boundary lemma, the count derivation and the Flock
  consequence lemma are in place.
\item \bndc{w.Constraints} is asserts and lookups only (Clean \bndc{93c9d1ef},
  \bndc{Clean/Circuit/Operations.lean:687-688}, probe \bndc{Shapes} output lines 154--159); leanISA
  emits no lookup and only \bndc{JUMP} asserts; so \bndc{toM3_constraints_iff} is provable in
  principle.
\item The degree bound \bndc{d = 2}: every flush coordinate of the six tables read
  (\bndc{LeanerVM/Arithmetization/Tables/*.lean}, \bndc{main}) is of degree at most two
  (\bndc{JUMP}'s successor \bndc{b·v_pc + b·(g·pc) + g·pc}, \bndc{Jump.lean:199-201}; \bndc{DEREF}'s
  store \bndc{fbar·v3 + f_pc·(g²·pc) + f_fp·fp}, \bndc{Deref.lean:203-206}; \bndc{MUL_NATIVE}'s twelve
  products, \bndc{MulNative.lean:168-173}; the pushes' \bndc{g · count}).
\item The state boundary as constants only (\bndc{Coord.committed} needs \bndc{τ = κ = 0},
  impossible for a real column), as \bndc{layout.rs:354-358}; the memory and bytecode blocks'
  committed coordinates are columns of tables whose \bndc{τ} equals the block's \bndc{κ} by
  construction (\cref{sec:gen-boundary-st-tables}).
\item \bndc{Caps} is derivable from \bndc{Admissible} plus the construction of \bndc{witnessOf} (the
  row of \bndc{caps} in \cref{tab:gen-boundary-conjuncts}), and \bndc{Sizes.ofWitness w = some s}
  from \bndc{SatisfiedBy} (\cref{sec:gen-boundary-completeness}).
\item The chain names one \bndc{prog} and one \bndc{input} throughout
  (\cref{sec:gen-boundary-other-program}); no theorem lets the prover choose either.
\item The top limb is anchored (\cref{sec:gen-boundary-toplimb}), agreeing with the public-input
  dossier's section D.
\item \bndc{Refinement} accepts a \bndc{Type 1} target witness (probe \bndc{Transport}); the
  pointwise composition of the base theorem typechecks (its examples 3--4);
  \bndc{Extractor.Straightline.map} cannot serve (probe \bndc{UniverseFail}).
\item The axioms of every arithmetization declaration the chain will use
  (\bndc{assumptions_of_blake2sRowsValid}, \bndc{memRowOf_bindings}, \bndc{bytecodeRowOf_bindings},
  \bndc{bytecodeRowOf_decodes}, \bndc{verifier_pull_eval}, \bndc{verifier_push_eval},
  \bndc{rowAt_toElements}, \bndc{decode_eq_some_iff}, \bndc{assignmentRepresents_image}, the six
  tables, the two blocks, the verifier) and of the two master theorems, \bndc{bytecodeColumn_eval},
  \bndc{idxColumn_eval}: the kernel's three (probe \bndc{Shapes}, output lines 168--187);
  \bndc{map_option_valid}: two.
\end{itemize}
\end{sloppypar}
